transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Amira Gomez (Redwood Product), Jared Collins (Helixware CTO), Priya Rao (Helixware ML Eng), Martin Yoon (Helixware Infra), Sasha (Helixware Procurement)

Summary (auto): High-level parity demo and console tour. Covered API translation examples from OpenAI and Anthropic calls to Redwood API, discussed KV cache behavior, batching knobs in Optimize, and Dedicated sizing considerations. Action items captured.

00:00 - 00:28 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we'll do a 45 to 60 min walk through parity and then leave time for Qs. I'm Maya, AE on the account. Lucas is our SE and will drive the deep demo. Amira is joining for any product/optimize questions.

00:29 - 01:05 Jared: Thanks. I'm Jared, CTO. Priya and Martin are on the line. Our goal: move away from a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints and consolidate on something we can own/optimize, ideally with predictable costs and better latency. We also need to understand if Redwood will match our prompt outputs, conversational state, and embeddings.

01:06 - 01:40 Lucas: Great — high level we'll show three things: (1) API parity mapping (how typical OpenAI/Together/Anthropic calls map to Redwood API), (2) Console & Optimize features to tune batching, caching, quantization, and (3) the Dedicated/private patterns for your infra constraints.

01:41 - 02:15 Priya: Quick note — we use Together for some safety layers and OpenAI for chat. Tokenization differences have bitten us before; prompts that worked with OpenAI sometimes shift tokens with other tokenizers.

02:16 - 03:05 Lucas: Yep, totally. We'll show tokenization parity tips and a small tokenizer preview pane in the console. Also, there are a couple of subtle output deltas on sampling defaults — we'll show how to set deterministic temperature/seed equivalents.

03:06 - 04:02 Maya: Before we dive, any hard constraints? Regulatory? VPC? Data residency?

04:03 - 04:40 Martin: We need VPC peering and an option for on-prem later. Also SOC 2 compliance is non-negotiable. Latency target is p95 < 250ms for our short chat flows, and cost needs to be at least 20% lower than current spend.

04:41 - 05:10 Amira: Quick callout: we have private deployments with KMS integrations and audit logs — so that can be part of the path if you need on-prem or VPC. We'll show the VPC options in the console briefly.

05:11 - 06:00 Lucas (screen share): Okay jump to the API parity doc.

06:01 - 06:35 06:35 - Speaker 1: (mumble) — I think the screen flaked...

06:36 - 08:05 Lucas: Alright, so first example — an OpenAI chat.completions request: we show the role/messages mapping, temperature, top_p, max_tokens. In Redwood it's a single /v1/generate style call but we have compatibility helpers in the SDK. Example curl snippet: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model": "rwd-ggml-chat-13b", "messages": [...], "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.2 }' — note we also expose per-request routing hints if you want cheap vs low-latency.

08:06 - 09:00 Priya: How do streaming differences manifest? We've built UIs depending on OpenAI server-sent events.

09:01 - 09:40 Lucas: We support streaming via chunked HTTP and SSE; the payload shape is close but not identical. We have a small adapter in the SDK that normalizes event types to what your UI expects. Small caveat: streaming chunk granularity may differ if you use long context windows because of our batching pipeline.

09:41 - 11:10 Jared: Also, Anthropic has safety-specific fields (like `context` for system). How do we translate those?

11:11 - 12:20 Lucas: Good question — for Anthropic-ish semantics we map system context into messages and expose safety hooks in the console. There are a few heuristics we recommend for system vs user message placement to keep behavior consistent. We'll include sample mapping for Anthropic 'clauses' — sorry, I mean 'class' — the transcript garbled — we'll share exact examples.

12:21 - 13:05 Maya: Let's jump to the console — rollouts, routes, and tracing.

13:06 - 14:45 Amira (screen share): This is the Console view. On the left you can see Models, Routes, and Rollouts. For routes we can set pinning rules by header, path, or customer tier. For rollouts you get canary percentages, automatic fallback policies, and a traffic heatmap. Here is an example of a canary that sends 5% to a quantized variant.

14:46 - 15:30 Martin: Can we see token-level cost and tracing for a given API key? We need to attribute spend by route and team.

15:31 - 16:10 Amira: Yes — per-token breakdown by key and per-route charts. Traces will show memcache hits, routing decisions, and kernel selection if you want to dig into the p99 tail.

16:11 - 17:05 Lucas: Quick Optimize demo: We recommend three levers — batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles. For your usage we suspect batching + prefix caching will reduce token compute by ~30% with minimal quality drop.

17:06 - 18:20 Priya: How do you handle KV cache invalidation for chat sessions? Our sessions sometimes interleave with external state.

18:21 - 19:10 Lucas: We support session-scoped KV caches with TTL and manual invalidation APIs. Note: some customers call it K-V cash in older notes — transcript: there were some recognition errors.

19:11 - 20:00 Lucas: Also about quantization: we provide recommended quant profiles per model and allow you to run sample workloads in a sandbox to see perf/behaviour tradeoffs.

20:01 - 22:00 Jared: Any pitfalls migrating embeddings from OpenAI? We use embeddings for search/rerank and vector stores.

22:01 - 23:15 Lucas: Embedding dimension differences sometimes require reindexing. We have embedding parity guides and scripts to migrate vectors and re-embed. We'll share a small tool we've used in other migrations to compare cosine similarity distributions pre/post.

23:16 - 24:40 Martin: On networking/peering — what does VPC or private deployment look like? We need deterministic egress IPs and firewall allowlists.

24:41 - 26:05 Amira: For Private deployments we do a customer-controlled control plane plus a private data path; KMS integration for key wrapping, HSM optional. For Hosted we support VPC peering with static egress anchors; we'll include the network diagram in the docs drop.

26:06 - 27:30 Priya: Security: SSO and audit logs — is SAML/OIDC supported? And what about SOC2 reports?

27:31 - 28:20 Maya: Yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC role mapping, and audit logs. We are SOC2 Type II — Amira will drop the formal report and controls matrix after this call.

28:21 - 30:00 Lucas: Back to parity: here's a rough mapping table — OpenAI messages -> Redwood messages; Anthropic context -> system messages; Together sampling params -> Redwood temperature/top_p equivalents. Also note differences in default max context handling, we expose chunking helpers. Example snippet for sampling parity: set temperature and top_p explicitly, and pin seed for deterministic tests.

30:01 - 31:05 Jared: What about fallbacks during capacity spikes? If we run Dedicated how do fallbacks to hosted work?

31:06 - 32:00 Amira: You can configure smart routing policies — prefer Dedicated for production but fall back to hosted regional pool with rate ceilings. There's also auto-quantize fallbacks if latencies spike.

32:01 - 33:10 Lucas: Demo: run a small benchmark — we replayed one of your short chat flows (sanitized). P95 was ~210ms with small batching and a quantized variant at 180ms but with a tiny divergence in stop tokens on one prompt. We kept the exact logs in the sandbox.

33:11 - 34:05 Priya: That one divergence — is it reproducible? We need determinism for some of our assistant flows.

34:06 - 35:20 Lucas: We saw it on a high-length scenario; recommend pinning sampling params and using a higher precision profile for those flows. For most short interactions the quantized profile showed parity within your human eval thresholds.

35:21 - 36:40 Jared: Pricing model — we need to understand hosted per-token vs Dedicated commitment math.

36:41 - 38:00 Maya: Pricing overview: hosted is usage-based per-token plus optional retention addons; Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool with a fixed monthly commit and overage unit pricing. We'll send a rough TCO calc in the parity spreadsheet. Our goal is to show you where batching/optimize cuts unit cost so you can see the delta to your current spend.

38:01 - 39:10 Sasha: Procurement question — what's the typical lead time for Dedicated onboarding and SOW?

39:11 - 40:20 Maya: Dedicated onboarding typically 4–8 weeks depending on networking and compliance. We'll include an SOW template. For POC you can start with Hosted plus a traffic replay to bench.

40:21 - 42:00 Lucas: Last demo slide: Console Alerting and Eval hooks — you can attach evaluation prompts and quality monitoring per-rollout so regressions trigger alerts. This ties into Optimize so you can see cost vs quality.

42:01 - 43:20 Priya: Can we run a small POC: 2 week bench with a replay of 1 hour traffic and up to 100k tokens? What's the gating?

43:21 - 44:10 Maya: Yes, that's doable. We'll need an NDA in place and a small POC agreement. After you share replay we'll run the micro-bench and share results.

44:11 - 45:30 Martin: Firewall considerations — will you need inbound rules? Most of our cluster is air-gapped for PCI workloads.

45:31 - 46:20 Amira: For air-gapped we provide on-prem options; for VPC peering hosted will use egress allowlists. We'll follow up with a network checklist.

46:21 - 48:00 Lucas: Quick recap: we'll produce a parity mapping doc with concrete cURL/SDK mappings, a micro-benchmark plan, and a console tour recording. Also security packet (SOC2, SSO docs).

48:01 - 49:30 Maya: Next steps recap — Maya to share parity sheet, Lucas to propose bench run times, Amira to drop security artifacts, Helixware to share tokenization examples and replay.

49:31 - 50:20 Jared: Sounds good. Any other questions?

50:21 - 51:05 Priya: One more — embedding dimension drift: do you provide a recommended re-index strategy?

51:06 - 52:00 Lucas: Yes — small batched reindex and cosine similarity sanity checks. We'll attach the reindex script sample. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the artifacts.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription artifacts: speakers occasionally labeled generically; some proper nouns were misrecognized (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "sock-two" for SOC2). There are short filler words and overlap in a few segments.
